observations: body L1-L3: the end of the sentence on Henry Bate begun on p. 314. «celi» (L2) is printed so. A speck stands under the closing quotation mark of L3, like a colon.

body L4-L13: «al–Battānī» (L4) and «Ptolemaeus», divided between L11 and L12, are letter-spaced; the long dash of «al–Battānī» measures 5.2 pt. Al-Battānī's special book on these ascensions is the one spoken of in the preface. On the meridian the circle of position of a degree is the meridian, and on the horizon it is the horizon (notes 1 and 2), so the difference of right, or of oblique, ascensions gives the direction only in these places, as printed.
body L14-L17: the dash before «Sit» (L17) measures 9.6 pt.

body L18-L31: the figure of the sphere stands on the right of L18-L31, redrawn from the print: the horizon, the circle of position NAS, the equator and the ecliptic as circles fitted to the printed strokes (rms 0.29 to 0.32 pt), the meridian NS as a straight stroke; the dashed parallels FF′, EE′ and the dashed circles of declination from P through B, C, A, E and F are fitted to their dashes and drawn dash by dash; the arc bc of the equator is printed bold, the line thickened upward over its length, and the arc BC of the parallel EE′ bold; the points P, A, B are marked by dots, B with a cross. The words horizon, ecliptica and aequator are set letter by letter along their circles, meridianus upright along the meridian; the sign of Aries stands on the meeting of the equator and the ecliptic. The dash after «I.» (L24) measures 5.5 pt, a long dash, with a point printed before it. «al–Battānī» (L22) is letter-spaced, with a long dash (5.4 pt).

body L32-L39: the minus signs of the formula (L32) are printed as dashes (9.2 to 10.2 pt) and set as minus signs; the sign of Aries is printed in a form like a V. The formula is right: ♈a and ♈b are the right ascensions of A and B, the arc ♈c of the equator, which is ♈a − ca, is the right ascension of C, and C lies on the parallel of B, so bc = ♈c − ♈b. When A is on the horizon at F, c falls at β and a at α, and ca = βα = Dα − Dβ, the difference of the semidiurnal arcs of A and B, as printed. «al–Battānī» (L39) is letter-spaced, with a long dash (5.4 pt); «10–36» has a long dash (5.2 pt). The o of «oritur» (L39) prints broken, like a c.
notes_left L1-L7: note 3, by Schiaparelli, goes on on p. 316. A speck stands before «deberet» (L7).
